canonical_policy.name: Shared UoW context and no repository container
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Repositories in one use case share the same scoped Unit of Work/DbContext; IUnitOfWork must not become a repository container or service locator.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Shared scoped Unit of Work/context, explicit repository injection and no container/service-locator use match. Shared registration example adds no distinct requirement.

context_quotes:
- `IUnitOfWork` is the normal commit boundary of an Application use case: repositories stage changes, and Application Services decide when to commit (default).
- Repositories participating in one use case must share the same scoped Unit of Work and persistence context. Repositories are injected explicitly into their consumers; `IUnitOfWork` must not become a repository container or service locator.
- Do not introduce explicit transaction APIs until a concrete use case requires control beyond the normal single save/commit (default).

- Entity mappings live in Infrastructure as `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` classes, keeping persistence configuration out of Domain entities where practical (prefer).
- The Infrastructure implementation of `IUnitOfWork` delegates to the same scoped `DbContext` that the use case's repositories share.
- An Infrastructure-only `Repository<TEntity>` base class may expose protected helpers to concrete repositories; concrete repositories may use the full EF Core API internally.
Repositories share the scoped `AppDbContext` because it is registered scoped and injected into each of them.
Lazy loading by default; fire-and-forget EF async calls.

canonical_policy.name: Explicit transactions only for real need
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Do not introduce explicit transaction APIs until a concrete use case requires control beyond normal SaveChangesAsync.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Concrete multi-operation atomicity trigger and Infrastructure transaction location match; not a requirement to add transactions for every operation, nor a solution for distributed atomicity.

context_quotes:
- Repositories participating in one use case must share the same scoped Unit of Work and persistence context. Repositories are injected explicitly into their consumers; `IUnitOfWork` must not become a repository container or service locator.
- Do not introduce explicit transaction APIs until a concrete use case requires control beyond the normal single save/commit (default).

A single `SaveChangesAsync` is the normal transaction boundary for one operation. When a concrete use case needs several operations or several saves to succeed atomically, use `await using var tx = await db.Database.BeginTransactionAsync(cancellationToken);` … `await tx.CommitAsync(cancellationToken);` inside Infrastructure. EF transactions do not solve distributed transactions.

canonical_policy.name: EF Core is Infrastructure detail
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Use EF Core normally inside Infrastructure but do not leak EF Core concepts into Application.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Normal full EF usage and no crippling generic facade match. Mapping organization BF0027, tracking/lazy-loading BF0079 and migration project/startup location already registered.

context_quotes:
- The persistence framework is an Infrastructure implementation detail. Use it normally inside Infrastructure and take advantage of its capabilities, but do not leak its concepts into Application.
- Do not cripple repository implementations merely to preserve a generic abstraction; the repository boundary keeps persistence concerns out of Application, it does not hide the framework from Infrastructure.

- `DbContext`, `DbSet<T>`, EF Core APIs and LINQ-to-EF expressions, EF attributes and mapping types, and SQL Server provider types are persistence-framework types for the purposes of the Level 1 boundary rules.
- Entity mappings live in Infrastructure as `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` classes, keeping persistence configuration out of Domain entities where practical (prefer).

- **Seed data:** whenever a Domain or persistence change affects seeded entities (new required or renamed properties, changed relationships or enum/status values, new meaningful states, changed invariants), update the maintained development seeder in the same change so that recreating the Development database at this revision yields valid, representative data (`3-project/data-lifecycle.md`).
- **Migrations:** create schema changes as new EF Core migrations from the Infrastructure project with the Api project as startup project, for example `dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project backend/<Name>.Infrastructure --startup-project backend/<Name>.Api`. Treat migrations as source code: review each generated migration before committing it, paying particular attention to destructive schema changes, unexpected column recreation, data migrations, indexes, foreign keys, and delete behavior.
- **Tests:** changed behavior gets maintained automated coverage at the right level (`0-core/testing-principles.md`).

- Use tracking queries when loaded entities will be modified and committed through the current Unit of Work; use `AsNoTracking()` for read-only entity queries where tracking adds nothing. Projections to non-entity DTOs do not need `AsNoTracking()`.
- `FindAsync([orderId], cancellationToken)` fits primary-key lookups where an entity instance is needed and an already tracked instance is acceptable; use LINQ for extra predicates, projection, related data, or shaping.

## Related data

Prefer an explicit query shape: projection for selected related data, `Include`/`ThenInclude` when the graph itself is needed. Avoid lazy loading by default — it hides database access and invites N+1 queries. For large collection includes consider split queries and verify the generated SQL.

Interceptors suit infrastructure cross-cutting behavior such as auditing, not hidden business behavior:

Prefer explicit registrations in small and medium projects; scan when registration volume creates genuine boilerplate, and scan the assembly that owns the services (not accidentally only the Api assembly):

```csharp
builder.Services.Scan(scan => scan
    .FromAssemblyOf<IOrderService>()
    .AddClasses(c => c.AssignableTo<IScopedService>())
    .AsImplementedInterfaces()
    .WithScopedLifetime());
```

## Factory delegates

```csharp
builder.Services.AddScoped<IPaymentProcessor>(sp =>
{
    var config = sp.GetRequiredService<IOptions<PaymentOptions>>().Value;
    return config.Provider switch
    {
        "stripe" => ActivatorUtilities.CreateInstance<StripeProcessor>(sp),
        "paypal" => ActivatorUtilities.CreateInstance<PayPalProcessor>(sp),
        _ => throw new InvalidOperationException($"Unknown payment provider: {config.Provider}")
    };
});
```

## Scoped work from singletons

A singleton or hosted service that needs scoped work creates a scope per operation and resolves a scoped orchestration service — not Infrastructure internals:

Registering an Application service that uses repositories/Unit of Work as a singleton is a captive-dependency bug: register it scoped.

| Scenario | Technique |
|---|---|
| Application service using repositories/UoW | scoped |
| Stateless helper without scoped dependencies | transient or concrete registration |
| Immutable shared configuration | singleton-compatible |
| `DbContext` | scoped (`AddDbContext`) |
| Several implementations selected by key | keyed services |
| Cross-cutting wrapper | decorator |
| Many repetitive registrations | Scrutor scanning |
| Runtime implementation selection | factory delegate |
| Strongly typed configuration | `AddOptions<T>().BindConfiguration()` (`configuration` skill) |
Do not capture a transient typed client inside a singleton without understanding the lifetime implications. Choose keyed clients only when keyed DI makes consumption clearer.

canonical_policy.name: Registration stays near the owning layer
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Keep registration close to the owning layer: Application registers Application services, Infrastructure registers persistence/adapters, and API remains the composition root.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Owner-layer registration, validator assembly API, owned-assembly scanning, Application-only services/validation and Infrastructure list are explicit. No universal scanner inferred from illustrative code.

context_quotes:
- `Program.cs` in Api is the application composition root and may register Infrastructure implementations (default).
- Keep registration close to the owning layer: Application registers Application services, Infrastructure registers persistence and adapters, and Api remains the composition root (default).
- Use constructor injection for required dependencies by default; avoid service-locator and property-injection patterns (default).

- Use FluentValidation for explicit request and use-case validation where validation is needed — required application input, string and collection constraints, ranges, cross-property and conditional rules — while each rule stays at the owning boundary defined in `1-architecture/outcomes.md`.
- Application-level validators live in Application and are registered with `FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions` from Application's own registration.
- Follow the project's established validation invocation pattern rather than adding a second competing mechanism; do not adopt a deprecated or legacy ASP.NET automatic-validation integration package unless a concrete project requirement justifies it (default).

Register validators with `services.AddValidatorsFromAssemblyContaining<CreateOrderRequestValidator>()` (FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions) and invoke them through the project's one established mechanism (for example explicitly in the Application Service, or an action filter in Api).

```text
backend/<Name>.Application/
├── Abstractions/
│   ├── Persistence/          # ITaskRepository.cs, IOrderRepository.cs, IUnitOfWork.cs
│   └── ExternalServices/     # IEmailSender.cs, ICurrentUser.cs, IFileStorage.cs — only when needed
├── Services/                 # ITaskService.cs, TaskService.cs
├── DTOs/                     # operation/data models when useful — not a dumping ground
├── Validation/               # validators for Application input when needed
└── DependencyInjection.cs    # AddApplication(): Application services and validation only
```

`AddInfrastructure` registers `AppDbContext`, repository implementations, `IUnitOfWork`, external adapters, the SQL Server provider, `HttpClient` integrations, and resilience handlers when used. Create capability-specific subdirectories under `Services/` when they improve cohesion.

canonical_policy.name: Cache infrastructure does not leak inward
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Keep cache technology out of Domain and do not leak infrastructure cache APIs into Application without a deliberate boundary abstraction.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Cache boundary and conditional Application abstraction with Infrastructure-only exception match. Api output-cache location, preserved adapter contract and post-successful-commit invalidation explicitly represented.

context_quotes:
- Infrastructure translates remote HTTP responses into the Application-facing abstraction; do not leak `HttpResponseMessage` or other remote-transport concerns into Application.
- Keep cache technology out of Domain, and do not leak infrastructure cache APIs into Application without a deliberate boundary abstraction.

- **HTTP response caching** — ASP.NET Core output caching when the entire response can safely be reused; it belongs in Api.
- **Application/data caching** — when a use case genuinely needs cache-aware behavior, define an abstraction in Application and implement it in Infrastructure; skip the abstraction when caching can stay an Infrastructure detail.
- **Infrastructure caching** — adapters may cache expensive remote or persistence operations when the contract to Application is preserved.

Infrastructure may implement it with `HybridCache`, which stays behind the abstraction (`backend-layers.md`). Mutations still follow the normal repository/Unit of Work flow; remove or update the affected entry after the commit succeeded.
| Expensive repeated remote read | cache inside the Infrastructure adapter |
| Application-controlled invalidation | Application abstraction + Infrastructure implementation |
